title: Armstrong tells him on opening night: this is your band
summary: On the Greystone opening night Armstrong made Randolph take the band, embarrassing him when he stomped off seated, and he then directed sets whenever Armstrong rested.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, to really to get your -- to get the record straight about -- now, this band -- I joined Louie starting in Detroit. I made a jump out here -- this man, Johnny Lindsay and myself, see -- see, we joined Louie. I'll tell you why I'm sitting over there after awhile and not sitting here. I joined Louie in Detroit -- Johnny Lindsay and myself. The first night we opened up at the Greystone Ballroom -- I mean

Lindsay and myself opened up with Louie at the Greystone Ballroom Louie played up to a certain time, then he took a rest -- intermission. I always make a habit, when I take intermission and come back on the bandstand, say about five minutes before they hit -- ten minues, so I can just go back there and sit down. I don't really have to go -- back there and sit down, and when I went back, Louie hollered at me, "Hey Randy," and I says, "Yes." He said, "Pick you out a set and take it down. Now, this is your band."
That's what he said. "This is your band."

June in '31. I didn't think much of it, you know, what he said. I picked out a set and then -- no, he told me to -- that's right, he called them in -- so I called da-da-da-da- -- so they came. "Pick out a set." And they all sat there (unintelligible) I picked out a set. "Go ahead and take down the set now, this is your band." When he said that, why, they all looked at one another. But I didn't think nothing of it, you know. So, I picked out a set and I always give them a signal to get ready. One -- that means for everybody to get in position. And I stomped off -- I stomped off sitting down.
Ready? One, two, three, four -- (unintelligible) and the people were all standing, looking, you know. And that embarrassed me.

I can't repeat the words -- get up from there and blank the blank and stand in front of the stand. I jumped up, you know, and embarrassed, but I jumped up and one of those things commenced directing the band -- one of those things. And I was looking at the folks, you know, (unintelligible) because that's the way I direct the band. I don't turn my back to them all the time.

And I turned around -- well, I turned around and looked into these guys' faces and they looked at me and they looked like they could [ ], see. Right there. Well, I didn't pay too much attention to that then. Well, we went on -- as we went on -- I had charge of the band from then on. I would have to take charge of the band. Sometimes Louie would play down a set and then Louis would take his horn and walk off and then I got it and I'd have to stand up and play --
Yes, take Louie's place and stand up.
